rationale: Consolidated the catalog family into one successor crate.
Canonical catalog output is covered as a library contract and fixed-point test rather than a donor dump binary.
Cycle paths and structured diagnostics remain library behavior.
Lock drift is tested through typed findings instead of a dump-only executable.
Iterative deterministic cycle detection and reverse transitive dependents are preserved.
Entries, stable identity metadata, dependencies, material payloads, lookup, and canonical order are preserved under successor naming.
Kind-and-context fallback, fail-closed, and skip decisions are preserved.
The hand parser is replaced by strict serde DTOs with canonical ordering, nested unknown-field rejection, semantic paths, and fixed-point evidence.
The public behavior family is re-exported from a thin successor root.
Canonical lock generation, strict lock codec, and complete drift classification are preserved.
Authority and visual definitions still project into disjoint collision and render types.
Visual, authority-impacting, and structural change impacts and dependent revalidation are preserved.
Duplicate, payload, wrong-kind, missing dependency, cycle, and source-path failures remain typed and gain narrow serializable diagnostics.
Compact voxel material bindings, visual fallback, collision failure, and used-material validation are preserved.
Meaningful codec, cycle, lock, and strict-decoding regressions are consolidated into focused behavior tests; donor text formatting is not an authority.
Material change classification and reload suggestions are asserted structurally rather than through a presentation-only text golden.
Abstract fixture behavior is retained locally without exporting donor test helpers.
The separate protocol crate is consolidated into the behavior owner.
Stored references, catalog/material/lock shapes, stable diagnostic codes, and fallback semantics are exposed narrowly by the owning crate without global vocabulary tables or code generation.
